page: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dlsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of x86_64 system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor includes a large 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8), which accelerate vector and matrix operations. Cryptographic tasks are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32ls_v7 demonstrates strong performance in single-threaded and multi-threaded operations. It achieves top-tier results in Geekbench text processing and small-model LLM text generation. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the strong tier. Memory bandwidth tests show high throughput for cached small-block reads and stable performance for uncached large-block reads.

Given its low-memory configuration relative to the high-frequency 32-vCPU count, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The absence of local storage and GPUs makes it highly specialized for CPU-bound tasks. It is well-suited for web serving, software compilation, text processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference using small to medium models.
